name: opencode
one_liner: A free, open-source AI assistant that writes and edits code for you, similar to Cursor or GitHub Copilot but one you run and control yourself.
buyer: An IT department or dev-tools startup that wants an AI coding assistant without paying per-seat licensing to a closed vendor, or that needs the code to never leave their own servers.
business_use_cases: A dev-tools company forks it to build a branded, hosted coding-agent product for a specific niche, such as game development or embedded systems.
An enterprise with strict data-residency rules self-hosts it so proprietary source code never touches a third-party vendor's servers.
A coding bootcamp bundles it into its curriculum as a free AI pair-programmer so students don't need a paid Copilot seat.

money_ideas.idea: Offer a hosted, managed version with team features like SSO and usage dashboards as a paid add-on on top of the free open-source core.
Build and sell a vertical-specific fork tuned for one language or stack as a licensed product to enterprises in that niche.

steal_this: Run it against your own repo this weekend, note exactly where it struggles, and build a paid plugin or config pack that fixes that specific gap for one framework.
